existing_pattern_updates.reason: R5 identifies a historically pre-2004 Navy schedule with short retention for CIC logs and some routine EW-related records, while RB47 and Tehran remain split across multiple archival/custody surfaces.

N1-NU-89-005 predates the Nimitz event and assigns finite retention to SSIC 3560 Combat Information Center Logs and portions of SSIC 3610-3613 record families. The exact AN/SPY-1 raw-data classification remains unresolved, so case-specific destruction is not established.
R5 recovered no calibration/error model for the preserved numerical claims in RB47, Tehran or Nimitz.
No common-time calibrated multi-sensor data were recovered.

new_patterns.name: High-interest events span multiple records owners and record classes
new_patterns.definition: The strongest residuals distribute potentially relevant evidence across different operational units, sensors, agencies, record schedules and national custodians, so a single FOIA/archive search can legitimately recover only a narrative subset.

case_notes.RB47_1957: Potential records span Project Blue Book, OSI, Air Defense/radar units and aircraft/ELINT reporting channels.
case_notes.NIMITZ_2004: Potential records span USS Princeton CIC/AEGIS, E-2C, air wing/air-defense communications and multiple Navy records/FOIA components.
case_notes.TEHRAN_1976: Potential records span DIA/JCS, USDAO Tehran, State/RG59, Defense/RG330 and Iranian IIAF/Mehrabad custody.

ordinary_explanations: different records schedules by data class
new_patterns.discriminating_measurement: Build a custody graph for each sensor/data class with named originating unit, records owner, schedule, transfer path and disposition state.
new_patterns.epistemic_ceiling: Custody fragmentation explains missing fusion data; it says nothing by itself about the physical origin of the reported target.

new_relationships.relation: More independent military sensors usually means more independent records owners, classifications and retention rules; evidential richness can therefore increase archival fragmentation.
When sensor channels are owned and retained separately, post-event narratives may correlate them while raw common-time fusion becomes unavailable.
Different components can apply different schedules to neighboring data classes, making partial survival of reports alongside loss of tactical data unsurprising.

hypothesis_effects.reason: Another iteration added evidence-pipeline structure but no repeated calibrated physical property.
The top residuals remain unresolved, but R5 supplied no new physical measurement requiring a common unknown platform.

canonical_seal: R5 FOUND A REPEATING ORGANIZATIONAL SIGNATURE, NOT A MACHINE SIGNATURE: THE MORE CHANNELS A CASE HAS, THE MORE CUSTODY PATHS MUST SURVIVE BEFORE THE PHYSICS CAN BE REPLAYED.
